packet.first_task: A repair café needs a notice for a first-time visitor bringing a lamp. Visitors bringing a lamp use the side door by 6 p.m. Friday. Volunteers use the main entrance. The draft reads, 'Please come to the usual entrance by the deadline.' Write your version for that visitor, then explain one edit in terms of what the reader needs. Choose your own voice.
packet.goal: I want to learn how to be a better writer

response.first_answer:
Bringing a lamp to the repair café? Please use the side door and arrive by 6 p.m. Friday.

I changed “the usual entrance” to “the side door” because a first-time visitor wouldn’t know which entrance we usually use.
response.return_request: Can we try two versions of the lamp notice, one with the line about volunteers and one without? I want to see which is easier to scan.
response.surprise: I almost added “Volunteers use the main entrance” because I pictured a visitor seeing people go in there and following them. I left it out because I pictured my notice taped beside the main door, where the lamp instruction would be the first thing they saw. Yes, please save writing clear directions for first-time readers as a topic.
